text:
### Observed differences

- A25 and A26 remained present in all observed traces in both windows. A25 was before A28-A34 in about 49-52 in 100 traces earlier and about 98-100 in 100 later, while A26 was after A28-A34 in about 49-52 in 100 traces earlier and about 98-100 in 100 later. [POS001, POS002, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012]
- A28, A30 and A31 occurred in about 49 in 100 traces earlier and about 99 in 100 later, while A32, A33 and A34 occurred in about 52 in 100 traces earlier and about 100 in 100 later, with no repeated occurrences. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]
- Earlier, the A28/A30/A31 group and the A32/A33/A34 group were alternatives: for example, A28 and A32 co-occurred in 0 in 100 traces, with A28 alone in about 49 in 100 and A32 alone in about 52 in 100. In the later window, A28 and A32 co-occurred in about 98 in 100 traces, and A28, A30 or A31 was before A32, A33 or A34 in about 98 in 100 of those co-occurring traces. [REL015, REL016, REL017, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024]
- Within each group, the order remained mixed: earlier and later, A28/A30/A31 appeared in both orders in similar proportions, and A32/A33/A34 appeared in both orders in similar proportions. [REL013, REL014, REL018, REL025, REL026, REL027]
- A25's outgoing routing changed from roughly equal choices among A28-A34 (about 15-19 in 100 of observed outgoing transitions) to mainly A28, A30 and A31 (about 30-38 in 100), with A32 and A34 at about 1 in 100 or less and A33 not observed among A25's outgoing transitions. [DIR001]
- A28, A30 and A31 previously led to A26 in about 30-36 in 100 of observed outgoing transitions; in the later window they led to A32, A33 and A34 in about 8-13 in 100 of observed outgoing transitions and to A26 in about 0-1 in 100. [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]
- Event positions moved consistently with a longer middle section in event positions: A25's mean position fell from about 0.67 to about 0.62, A26's rose from about 0.80 to about 0.83, A28-A31 moved earlier (mean about 0.74 to about 0.68), and A32-A34 moved later (mean about 0.73 to about 0.77). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008]
- Where pairs occurred within five event steps, the distance from A25 to A32-A34 and from A28/A30/A31 to A26 shifted from 1-3 steps to mostly 4-5 steps. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

- The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, the two previously alternative middle groups became a single near-mandatory sequence: A28, A30 and A31 are executed first in no fixed order, followed by A32, A33 and A34 in no fixed order, between A25 and A26. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, REL025, REL026, REL027, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006]
- Supporting signs are that all six middle activities rose from about half to nearly all traces, cross-group co-occurrence rose from 0 to about 98 in 100, cross-group order became A28/A30/A31 before A32/A33/A34, A25 now routes into the first group, the first group now routes into the second group, and event-position distances lengthened accordingly. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, REL025, REL026, REL027, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006]
- The main competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the later window contains a different mix of cases or that the two groups were already connected but only rarely sampled; the consistent participation, relation, routing and position changes across the same activities make this less likely but do not exclude it. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, REL025, REL026, REL027, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006]
